Cautiously hawkish with a stronger credit headwind. The FOMC raised the target range to 4.75–5% and continued QT, emphasizing “cumulative tightening,” policy lags, and the likelihood that recent banking stresses will tighten credit and weigh on activity, hiring, and inflation, while noting the system is “sound and resilient.” Beige Book anecdotes across districts (Boston, New York, Philadelphia, Atlanta, Dallas, San Francisco) point to softer regional economic activity: retailers, restaurants, and manufacturers report weaker demand; housing markets in New York and San Francisco are cooler; and wage growth remains above average in some areas (e.g., Boston) even as hiring plans become more cautious. These qualitative signals align with SLOOS evidence of broad-based tightening in C&I and CRE and weaker loan demand, implying a more pronounced contraction in credit availability than the policy statement alone suggests. Netting these, the communication remains restrictive, but Beige Book plus SLOOS tilt the balance further toward downside risks for growth and employment and gradual easing in inflation pressures.
